prompts: Use case: product-mockup / precise-object-edit. Redesign the attached Fold Wing Buddy into ONE new mechanically articulated AI study-coach lighting robot. Retain cream rounded central friendly face with camera shutter, microphone, fabric speaker belly, stable low base, phone dock, sage accents, workbook and warm home desk setting. RADICAL ARM REDESIGN REQUIRED: eliminate the continuous smooth plastic curved arches entirely. There must be exactly TWO arms, each built from distinct short rigid links with exposed-looking but covered motor housings, clear assembly seams, screw fasteners and neat cable loops, no extra tiny green arms, no projectiles. Each arm has exactly TWO powered ROTARY JOINTS: J1 at its shoulder/base is a visibly vertical-axis yaw turntable, J2 at its elbow is a visibly horizontal-axis pitch hinge. No independent wrist hinge, and no extra rotary joints. Left and right arms each visibly have only J1 and J2, oriented at different angles to demonstrate real mobility. Use dark gray joint housings contrasting ivory structural links, segmented NeoPixel accents on the rigid links. The end of each arm is a friendly stylized HAND LAMP: a round palm housing with a down-facing light optic and four short rounded fixed finger silhouettes plus a short fixed thumb along its outer edge. Fingers are integral fixed non-articulated design lobes, not additional driven joints, and hand is rigidly mounted to its last link. PALM OPTICAL ACTUATOR: show a small distinct linear motor/lead-screw carriage parallel to the optical axis moving the lens group in a short telescoping zoom barrel; the glass lens and lens movement seam should be visibly understandable. This is separate from the TWO arm rotary joints. LEFT hand lamp aims a tight brighter spot onto ONE exercise region on the left workbook page, RIGHT hand lamp aims a wider softer illumination pool onto another page region. Preserve readable paper texture, gentle ambient room light; illustrate two different beam footprints, not lasers and not floating flashlight beams. The robot should look capable of waving its hand lamps to attract attention and then aiming at a worksheet, not like a static arch lamp. Camera is slightly higher 3/4 angle to show both hands' palms, joint axes and the two distinct light pools on the workbook. Sophisticated photorealistic manufacturable concept rendering, landscape 3:2, entire product and page in frame. Add a few clean unobtrusive engineering-style callouts ONLY with exact short labels 'J1 YAW', 'J2 PITCH', 'LENS ACTUATOR', 'SPOT', 'WIDE' and slim leader lines; duplicate J1/J2 labels once per arm if possible. Avoid humanoid flesh hands, sharp fingers, extra wrists, third powered arm joints, smooth unbroken arch wings, collages, logos or watermarks. This is a mechanical design concept, not a functioning or validated product.

Precise mechanical correction to this exact product concept. Preserve entire composition, two hands with fixed finger design, friendly central body, camera, phone, elbow J2 PITCH joints, telescoping LENS ACTUATOR optics and SPOT/WIDE worksheet lighting. Change ONLY both lower J1 YAW joints: they are currently side-facing cylinders resembling pitch joints. Replace each lower joint with an unmistakably VERTICAL-AXIS YAW TURNTABLE: broad horizontal circular bearing disk on the base, dark low cylindrical motor underneath with vertical shaft, arm's lowest rigid link attached to a bracket rising from the top of the rotating platter. Show a subtle horizontal circular rotation arrow around each platter, J1 YAW labels lead directly to these turntables. No side-facing circular hinge/motor at J1. Each arm has exactly two powered rotational joints: this vertical yaw base, and the existing horizontal J2 pitch hinge next to hand lamp. No wrist hinge, no extra degree of freedom. Retain realistic screw fasteners, tidy cabling, fixed rounded fingers on hand lamp, separate optical zoom actuator, status LEDs and same photorealistic product identity. Do not add anything else or change layout.
status: Concept rendering; actual reach, illumination and mechanism performance unverified
